openingMessage: You're going to pay a price for everything you do and everything you don't do.
openingWhy: The bleed-down check costs ten minutes. Skipping it costs whatever the well decides to charge — and the field sets brutal prices. In Odessa it was two lives for one monitor left in the truck. There's no free option. Just the small bill now, or the one nobody can pay.
leadershipThought: Situational awareness is not a skill. It's a habit. You build it before you need it. The drive to location is the first job of the day — and the most dangerous thing most of us will do all week.

specialFocus.title: Week in Review — Confined Space · Atmospheric Monitoring
specialFocus.why: This morning is a look back before we roll forward. Last week was Confined Space week with Caleb hosting — and it was also the week this program started paying people back: the first monthly awards went out, the October trailer reset landed, and Matt's full September compliance review hit the board. Today we close that week out clean. The NEW topic — Driving & Journey Management, with Alex hosting — kicks off TOMORROW at full strength. Wednesday's wet-roads spotlight was the preview; tomorrow it becomes the whole show.
specialFocus.standardLabel: The Week That Was — Close It Out Clean
standard: The work: through Wednesday's export, 44 jobs and 86 forms with just 4 crew-raised flags — and every flag got talked through at a morning meeting. (Thursday and Friday's form exports are still pending — their numbers land on the board when the export catches up.)

October changeover: every trailer was due for the day-one flip — new inspection sheets, workpacks, mask bags opened and re-tagged, SCBA paperwork current. Leads: if any trailer in your lane is still showing September paperwork, it gets flipped TODAY, not re-discussed.

First Monthly Awards went home: Pablo Soto (backpack — 10 of 10 complete packets), Jacob Hernandez & Jose Campos (duck — 2 positive catches and an eagle on their joint forms), Jeremy Norris (attitude — Mike's pick). The Wall of Fame is live on the hub; October's race started Thursday.

Matt's September review is on the Job Forms tab: day forms held at 88.6%, but night forms fell to 40.3% and XTO trailer readiness sat at 68%. Those two gaps are October's coaching priorities — if you run nights or move trailers, you own one of them.

Standards set last week that don't expire with it: recognition names the person AND the behavior (Friday), and every shift change is a SPOKEN handoff — status, gas history, hazards, contacts (Saturday). Both are now how we operate.

Tomorrow, Tuesday: Alex hosts Day 1 of Driving & Journey Management. Driving is the most dangerous thing we do — come with your routes, your radar habit, and the wet-roads standard fresh from Wednesday.
